purpose: Teach: ケチ/熱気/喋る/注ぐ/末尾/相棒/やわらかい/おやすみなさい

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ケチに見られないようにしてた。
lines.en: When I was young, I made sure not to look like I was being cheap.
lines.style: Quiet, looking back across decades. Measured pace, slight pause before the admission. Matter-of-fact but with an undercurrent of old self-judgment. Voice settles into acceptance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。試合の熱気、二人で行ったのよね。
lines.en: Yes. The excitement of that game — we went together, didn't we.
lines.style: Warm recognition, nostalgic smile in the voice. Gentle emphasis on 「二人で」 — the togetherness matters most. Slightly trailing, savoring the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 孫と喋る時間、何より大事だ。
lines.en: Time talking with my grandchildren — there's nothing more important than that.
lines.style: Simple conviction. Not emphatic, but grounded. Slow and deliberate, like he's speaking something he's learned through living. Soft landing on the final word.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お茶、上手に注ぐのは、まだあなたが上ね。
lines.en: Your tea pouring — you're still the better one at it.
lines.style: Playful gentle teasing, the kind between people who know each other completely. Warm, almost a small laugh underneath. Light and easy, no sting.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 手紙の末尾、お前への愛、いつも書いていた。
lines.en: At the end of my letters, I was always writing my love for you.
lines.style: Quiet and steady, no performance. Vulnerable but not fragile. Slight pause before naming it. Voice opens on 「愛」, then settles. The kind of confession that only comes after seventy years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 人生の相棒、あなたで本当によかった。
lines.en: You as my life's partner — I was truly glad it turned out that way.
lines.style: Deep warmth, spoken like a benediction. Slow, each word given its weight. No breathlessness — just the peace of certainty. Trailing softly into the quiet between them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 今日のお布団、やわらかいね。
lines.style: Simple observation, almost to himself. Quiet, contented. The voice of someone noticing small comforts and feeling safe enough to name them. No elaboration — just presence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.style: The closing blessing of someone who has said good night a thousand times and means it every time. Warm, complete. A small breath of tenderness on the final word.
